Hub/Marketing/Newsletter
Marketing

Newsletter.

The marketing newsletter: an email a man chose to get, about health in plain words. It shares the build of the system emails and keeps the same discretion: nothing in the inbox says what he is treated for, or what he is curious about.

RulesConsentTemplatesMobileSubject linesLaunch calendarBuild notesOpen items
Current

Double opt-in. A man is on the list only after he confirms by email. Open tracking is on, and it is disclosed twice: in the consent line at sign-up and in the footer of every issue. One issue for everyone: every subscriber gets the same issue until legal approves segmentation (U-28). Legal approves every issue before it is sent (R-121).

Proposed

The templates, the subject bank and the launch calendar are proposals; the open items are at the end of the page. Square brackets mark what is filled in later: [UPPER_CASE] is a merge tag the email platform fills for each person; [Sentence case] is a slot a writer fills before sending. Legal entity and postal address wait for O-01.

Rules.

The system email rules apply in full. These are added for the newsletter.

Consent first.

Only people who opted in get it. The sign-up is its own unticked choice, never bundled with an order or the assessment. Double opt-in (U-28).

Discreet in the inbox.

Sender name "unifiedmeds". Subject line and preview text never name a condition, a medicine, a symptom or a body part. Read them as if a partner or a colleague sees the notification.

One idea per issue.

One headline, one short article, one button. A second topic waits for the next issue.

Education, not promotion.

The editorial issue explains and points to the provider. An offer goes in the separate announcement template, at most once a month.

The footer, every time.

Why he gets it, the open and click tracking line, a visible one-click unsubscribe, email preferences, privacy, and the legal entity with a postal address (CAN-SPAM; O-01).

Accessible by default.

Live text, never text inside an image. Alt text on every image. Body 16px or larger, buttons 50px tall (44px is the floor), AA contrast, lang="en".

Calm frequency.

Proposed: one editorial issue a month, plus at most one announcement. Never two marketing emails in the same week.

The provider decides.

Any line that touches treatment says a licensed provider decides (R-64). Clinical text in the provider block is written by the clinical team.

No claims.

No benefit claims, success rates, statistics, reviews, testimonials or star ratings (R-67). No medicine names in heroes, subjects or next to a benefit (R-65).

No pressure and no invented offers.

No countdowns, "last chance" or exclamation marks. No price, discount or percentage that legal and operations did not approve; savings are a dollar amount per product (R-61).

Consent and the two lists.

The newsletter and the system emails are two separate lists, sent from the same sender name. A man can leave the newsletter and still get his order and provider emails.

  1. Sign-up

    An unticked box or a short form on the marketing site footer, or in account settings. The consent line says what he will get, how often, and that opens and clicks are counted.

  2. Confirm

    Double opt-in (decided). A plain confirmation email with one button. Until he confirms, he gets nothing else.

  3. Welcome

    A short welcome that repeats the frequency and links to preferences and unsubscribe.

  4. Monthly issue

    The editorial template. Unsubscribe takes one click and needs no sign-in.

CurrentConsent line at sign-up.

"Send me the unifiedmeds newsletter: one short email about men's health, [frequency]. We count opens and clicks to learn what is useful. Unsubscribe in one click at any time. Privacy notice." The box is unticked. Legal approves the final wording; the frequency waits for Avi.

CurrentTracking line in every footer.

"We count opens and link clicks on this email to learn which issues are useful. We never use them to guess anything about your health. Read more in our privacy notice." Already in both templates below, right under the line that says why he gets the email.

Templates.

True email HTML at 600 wide, built like the system emails: tables, inline styles, PNG logo, light only, hidden preview text. Open one on its own, or download it as a starting point for the email platform.

The offer block stays empty until approved.

No price, saving or end date is written in by design or marketing. Legal and operations fill it, or the block is deleted.

The provider block is never filled by marketing.

It is a placeholder until the clinical team writes and signs it. Without their text, the block is removed from the issue.

Mobile preview.

The same files at 390 wide. Below 480 the card padding drops to 20, the headline to 28/34 and the button runs full width. Most opens are on a phone.

Subject lines and preview text.

The subject bank for every issue. Ten pairs: the left two columns can be used as written; the third shows what never ships, kept on purpose as a wrong example (R-129). The same discretion holds for the system emails (R-108). Subject under 50 characters, preview under 90, sentence case, no exclamation marks, no emoji.

Launch calendar.

Four monthly themes for the launch, Sexual health only (U-04). Each issue is written for the category but its subject and preview stay neutral. Every article goes through clinical and legal review before it is sent.

Proposal · month 1How it works.

The four steps, in the website's words: tell us what's changed, a licensed provider reviews your information, receive a personalized care plan, stay supported. Nothing promised about timing until operations confirm it (R-68).

Build notes.

For the developer. Platform agnostic: the templates work in any email platform that accepts custom HTML.

PartRule
LayoutSame as the system emails: tables with role="presentation", inline styles, 600 wide, Mist page, Paper card with radius 16. One <style> block in the head carries the phone rules only; the email still reads well where it is stripped
LogoThe same PNG at 2x, 200 × 33 shown, alt "unifiedmeds" (logo-horizontal@2x.png). Host every image on the brand domain (O-01)
Hero image1200 × 600 JPG at 2x, under 200 KB, shown at 600 × 300 (200 tall on phones). Never text inside the image. The slot carries the exact <img> markup in a comment
TypeHeadline DM Serif Display 32/38 (28/34 on phones) with Georgia as the fallback; text Inter 16/24 with Helvetica and Arial as fallbacks; footer 13/20
ButtonOne Dark button per email: Teal-deep, Paper label, radius 5, 50 tall, built as a table cell; full width on phones
ColourLight only (color-scheme: light only in meta and CSS), exactly like the system emails. Test the logo and the hero in the Gmail and Outlook apps with dark mode on
Preview textA hidden first block, padded with zero-width spaces so body text never leaks into the inbox preview
Merge tags[FIRST_NAME] (fallback "there"), [UNSUBSCRIBE_URL], [PREFERENCES_URL], [VIEW_IN_BROWSER_URL], [PRIVACY_URL], [SIGNUP_DATE], [ISSUE_NUMBER], [ARTICLE_URL], [LANDING_URL], [HERO_IMAGE_URL], [HERO_ALT], [END_DATE]. Swap each for the platform's own syntax at set-up
Links and UTM?utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=nl-[yyyy-mm]-[issue-slug]&utm_content=[placement]. Placement uses the landing page data-cta words: lowercase, hyphens, named by position (hero, body, final, footer). The issue slug never names a condition or medicine; no name, email or ID in any URL
UnsubscribeA visible link in every footer plus the List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers for one-click unsubscribe. No sign-in to leave
TrackingOpen tracking and click tracking on (U-28). Both are disclosed in the consent line and in the footer of every issue. Opens and clicks are reported per issue, never joined to health data or used to choose who gets an issue
AudienceOne list, one issue for everyone (U-28). No segments by category or treatment until legal approves segmentation
SendingSender name "unifiedmeds"; a separate sending subdomain for marketing so newsletter reputation never touches order emails (O-01)
File namesImage files used in emails carry neutral names (no condition or product), because an image address can show in a preview. See file naming (R-126)
Plain textEvery issue ships with a plain-text version with the same words and links
TestGmail (web and app), Apple Mail (Mac and iPhone), Outlook (Windows and web), Android; at 390 wide and with images off
